WITH connector_classes AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, s.qualname, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.class_bases cb ON s.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  WHERE cb.base_name = 'SQLDatabase'
    AND s.file_id NOT IN (SELECT file_id FROM code.files WHERE is_test = TRUE)
    AND s.kind = 'class'
),
connector_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id, s.name AS method_name, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'method'
    AND s.file_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_classes)
    AND s.name NOT LIKE '_%'
),
connector_method_own AS (
  SELECT cm.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, cm.method_name, cm.file_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT cb.base_symbol_id) AS base_count
  FROM connector_methods cm
  LEFT JOIN code.class_bases cb ON cm.class_symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  GROUP BY cm.symbol_id, cm.method_name, cm.file_id
),
class_has_base AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_classes
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
)
SELECT cmo.class_symbol_id, cmo.method_name
FROM connector_method_own cmo
WHERE cmo.class_symbol_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM class_has_base)
  AND cmo.base_count > 0
ORDER BY cmo.class_symbol_id, cmo.method_name;

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: The corrected query fixes the column reference: connector_method_own now uses cm.symbol_id (the method's symbol_id, which equals the class symbol_id) instead of cm.class_symbol_id. The base count is computed by joining class_bases on the class's file_id matching cb.class_symbol_id. Only methods in classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase and have at least one base are returned.
sql:
WITH connector_classes AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, s.qualname, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.class_bases cb ON s.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  WHERE cb.base_name = 'SQLDatabase'
    AND s.file_id NOT IN (SELECT file_id FROM code.files WHERE is_test = TRUE)
    AND s.kind = 'class'
),
connector_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id, s.name AS method_name, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'method'
    AND s.file_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_classes)
    AND s.name NOT LIKE '_%'
),
connector_method_own AS (
  SELECT cm.symbol_id, cm.method_name, cm.file_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id) AS base_count
  FROM connector_methods cm
  LEFT JOIN code.class_bases cb ON cm.file_id = cb.class_symbol_id
  GROUP BY cm.symbol_id, cm.method_name, cm.file_id
),
class_has_base AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_classes
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
)
SELECT cmo.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, cmo.method_name
FROM connector_method_own cmo
WHERE cmo.symbol_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM class_has_base)
  AND cmo.base_count > 0
ORDER BY cmo.symbol_id, cmo.method_name;
